transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start off, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

Well… I guess what’s bringing me in is, my wife thinks I’m reading too much into things. And maybe that’s how it looks from the outside, I understand that. But for about a year now, there’ve been these late meetings at her work, and little changes in how her messages come through—wording, timing, small details—and she says it’s all just normal office stuff.

But it doesn’t feel random to me. It’s like the pieces line up too precisely, if that makes sense. Not in some dramatic way, but like there’s a pattern underneath it, almost like a private signal. Like she’s trying to tell me something without actually saying it directly.

I’ve gone over it a lot in my head, probably more than I should, but it’s hard not to when the same kinds of things keep happening. I’m not saying I have every answer, but I can’t just ignore it either. It feels like something is being communicated, and I’m the only one willing to actually notice it.

When these thoughts about your wife's hidden signals come up, do they feel like unwanted intrusions that you wish you could stop having, or do they feel like something you're certain is actually true?

They don’t feel like random unwanted thoughts, no. I mean, I don’t enjoy having them—I’d rather not be in this position, obviously—but it’s not like some thought pops into my head and I think, “Oh, that’s ridiculous, why am I thinking that?” It feels more like I’m noticing something that’s actually there.

My wife says the late meetings and the changes in her work messages are just normal office stuff, and maybe someone else would leave it at that. But over the past year, the timing, the wording, the little shifts… they line up too precisely to feel accidental to me. It feels like there’s a private signal in it, like she’s trying to tell me something she won’t say directly.

So I wouldn’t say I wish I could just stop having the thought, exactly. I wish the situation would be clear. But the thoughts come from what I’m seeing, and what I’m seeing feels real.

Aside from what's going on with your wife, have you generally found yourself distrustful or suspicious of other people—like friends, coworkers, or family—throughout your life, even before this past year?

I mean… not really in the way you’re asking, I don’t think. I wouldn’t describe myself as someone who walks around assuming everyone has bad intentions or anything like that.

I can be cautious, I suppose, like anyone. And in a school or work setting there are always little politics, misunderstandings, people leaving things out—so I notice details. But I don’t think I’ve spent my whole life feeling suspicious of friends or family or coworkers as a general rule.

This thing with my wife feels different to me. It’s not like I just distrust people automatically. It’s more that certain things have happened and I can’t unsee the pattern. But before all this… no, I don’t think I would’ve called myself a suspicious person.
Have you ever heard voices, sounds, or seen things that others couldn't hear or see, especially related to this situation with your wife or otherwise?

No… I don’t think so. Not in the sense of hearing a voice when nobody’s there, or seeing a person or something that other people can’t see. I haven’t had anything like that.

With my wife, it’s more about things that are actually there—messages, timing, the way something is worded, when meetings happen, that kind of thing. I know that probably sounds like I’m splitting hairs, but it’s not like I’m hearing her voice telling me something from another room, or seeing signs floating in the air or anything like that. It’s more that I notice the details and they seem to fit together.

I mean, sometimes I’ll replay things in my head, like a conversation or a text, but that’s just me thinking about it. It’s not a sound outside my head. So, no, I wouldn’t say I’ve heard or seen things other people couldn’t.

Aside from what's happening with your wife, have you noticed any other situations—at work, with friends, or in daily life—where you feel people are sending you hidden signals or communicating secret messages?

No, not really… I mean, I’ve thought about that because I know how it must sound when I talk about the messages and timing and everything. But it’s not like I’m walking around thinking my coworkers are encoding things to me, or that strangers are leaving signs, or that friends are secretly communicating in some hidden way.

This is pretty specifically about my wife. Her late meetings, the small changes in how her work messages are worded, the timing of when things happen—it’s that they’ve lined up over the past year in a way that feels too precise to just be normal office noise. She says it’s all ordinary work stuff, and I understand that’s what she says, but to me it feels like there’s something underneath it, like a private signal meant for me, something she won’t say directly.

But outside of that situation? I don’t think so. I don’t have that same feeling with people at work or friends or just out in daily life. It’s not a general thing for me.
